text:
Two goals in Thursday's loss to Montreal pushed Casey Mittelstadt to seven on the season, and with them came the trade chatter: Heavy floated him as the center of a package for Dylan Larkin, and The Hockey Writers called him "an interesting dilemma" for Boston.

The dilemma is real, because the numbers split in two. The process is good. He's producing nearly a full expected goal per 60 (the quality of his own chances), up from 0.67 last season, and the Bruins take 57% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on the ice. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 7.9 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 81st percentile among forwards.

The results are running well ahead of that. Seven goals on 4.4 expected, a 25% shooting rate, and Boston has scored 8.2 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Numbers like that rarely hold.

So: a useful middle-six center at 14:22 a night, playing a little above himself. His minutes have crept up lately. Whether they keep climbing when the shots stop going in is the thing to watch.
